Treating this case as ordinary yields an outside probability matching this long-run historical base rate.

This current episode resembles those periods due to the newly reported significant rainfall deficit and regional disparities in the 2026 monsoon season, combined with rising input costs that are forcing short-lived festive e-commerce discounts. However, this episode differs fundamentally from 2015-2016 and 2023 in that it is compounded by a simultaneous central bank rate hike to 5.5 percent under a 'calibrated tightening' stance, paired with declining central tax receipts and foreign investors offloading equities in September 2026. Unlike the prior episodes where rural distress was cushioned by fiscal levers or steady liquidity, the current environment shows distinct vulnerability where festive input costs are compounding agricultural supply shocks, pushing headline inflation decisively above the 5.0 percent threshold.
